goal_title: Book: Form Finding: Rules, Constraints and Possible Shapes — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in formfinding became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

book.title: Form Finding: Rules, Constraints and Possible Shapes

reading.arc: Form Finding follows one question through six halls: when a shape looks as though it found itself, which operation actually produced it, and what decided that it could stop. Descent puts the visitor at a STEP button and lets one downhill rule end three named ways (SMALL SLOPE, LEFT FRAME, STEP LIMIT) and in two different valleys from two beginnings. Catenary and Relaxation then pull apart a hand-drafted spline, a sampled cosh, and a finite relaxation, ending at a glass vessel that is a frozen duration. Equilibrium shows a balance encoded by arithmetic beside a pulse and a tower that test nothing; Annealing supplies the one rule that can leave a valley and then argues, through the two wells, that the deepest is not necessarily the wanted one. Forge closes on a detector: the pieces settle by physics, but height and stillness are the author's criteria for what counts. The sequence keeps faith with its stated truth (an accepted endpoint depends on the model and its stopping rule) by naming, in every hall, what its objects do not test.
holds: The stopping rule as refrain: SMALL SLOPE / LEFT FRAME / STEP LIMIT (Descent) → a frame budget and a chosen step count (Relaxation) → a final temperature, a step limit and a forced HOP (Annealing) → SMALL SLOPE versus BOUNDARY and a height-plus-stillness detector (Forge).
A growing inventory of operations recited at each close: drafted, evaluated, settled, encoded, searched, counted. Equilibrium opens by recapping it and Annealing's last section lists five of the six.

Honesty written into the objects themselves: the laundry plate ("This is not a gravity solver"), the truss board ("NO LOAD TEST"), the end-table plate ("No forces are solved"), the two wells' INTERPRET button. The prose leans on things in the world that say their own limits.
The science_screen coda in four halls: "no compatible live measurement" — a picture is not yet an instrument.
Gaudí's hanging model and its inversion, introduced at the laundry lines and returned to in Equilibrium under the same Huerta footnote.
The downhill point in three bodies: the lab's gold marker, the bench's yellow blob, the optimiser's ball — one rule, different stops.

hall_notes.note: The strongest hall: STEP before explanation, the sampled gradient as a pink arrow, the rule revealed as one line, two beginnings that stop at different costs, three named endings. Reads as a guided experiment and every number checks against descent_landscape_lab.gd. Its weakness is the floor: five retained comparison works stand behind the lab and the chapter gives half a sentence to one of them.

Separates a hand-drafted spline, sampled cosh lines with their mirrored arches, and two sampled minimal surfaces, insisting on what each does not do. Reads well in the hand (bead, catenoid and helicoid are all grabbable) and the code sits after the encounter. A few sentences slip into the author's voice ("a further encounter to build").

Live cloth with PASSES / RESET / WIND, a frozen lattice, a vessel that is a duration; the mean-versus-worst error is the hall's sharpest lesson and the fossil argument lands. Two facts are off: the vessel's no-collider claim, and numbers sourced from a wind-off run that the live readout will not show.

Inspect one arm, then read the crossover arithmetic: the mobile paragraph is exemplary, and the triangle and tower are deflated honestly. It re-introduces Gaudí as if new and carries an editorial aside about the room's "older notes".

The longest and most exact chapter: uphill acceptance, adaptive cooling and the forced hop are separated the way the code separates them, the wells are compared before INTERPRET, and the close turns against its own first sentence. Nothing needs correcting; the deep well could use the standing view the review already rendered.

A detector that wants height and stillness, an optimiser with a BOUNDARY ending, and a fine last instruction (build something useful the puzzle refuses). Half the length of its neighbours, no words for the forge machine that stands first past the spawn and gives the hall its name, and no gathering of the sequence before the handover.

stumbles: FormFinding_Relaxation: the chapter says the vessel has no collider and your body can walk through its wall; the working-tree code builds a trimesh skin with backface collision, so a headset visitor walks into glass.

FormFinding_Forge: the self_shaping_forge stands three cells from spawn announcing DESCENT TOWARD MAX Q and a readout that hits MAX Q, straight after Annealing taught the visitor to distrust exactly that, and the chapter says nothing about it.

FormFinding_Descent: a Perlin-terrain descent station, a glowing self-portrait well, a static tremble inset and a screen stand behind the lab unnamed; the tremble inset can be read as a running solver.
FormFinding_Descent and FormFinding_Relaxation: "the recorded desktop comparison" / "a matched desktop calculation" — the visitor in the headset has no desktop and wonders what was measured where.
FormFinding_Relaxation: told to read MEAN and WORST and then given figures from a wind-off 420-step run, the visitor sees different numbers on the driven live readout and cannot tell why.
FormFinding_Relaxation: "the amphora is what those choose" stops the reader at the chapter's most literal sentence.
FormFinding_Equilibrium: "the room's own older notes claiming it turns on a breath" refers to a file the visitor never sees.
FormFinding_Catenary / FormFinding_Equilibrium: "a further encounter to build", "those encounters are still to be built" read as the museum's to-do list rather than the visitor's chapter.
FormFinding_Equilibrium: Gaudí's hanging models are introduced as new two halls after the laundry lines introduced them with the same footnote.
FormFinding_Forge: the sequence ends on a 543-word hall that hands over to oscillation without gathering what the six halls did.

keep.quote: You can walk around the plot and see the other valley. That knowledge has not entered the algorithm merely because it has entered your view.
Nothing in the surface has announced that this much unfinished movement is acceptable. We supplied that threshold.
Watch for the difference between drawing an answer, evaluating an answer, and letting a system settle toward one.
The formula does not choose its own boundary. Somebody has already chosen the numbers from which it will begin.
The average has become small while one local relation is still far from its request. Look between those two numbers. What would we overlook if the bench reported only the reassuring one?
The heavier child rides the shorter arm because the arithmetic gives it no choice.
That second branch is annealing's central permission, and it is a strange thing to write down: a rule that sometimes accepts a worse outcome so that a local improvement need not become a prison.
Build a low arrangement that you find useful and the puzzle refuses. Describe its usefulness without pretending it passed.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace closes with "In the next sequence, Form Finding, that question reaches the shape of the world itself", and Descent opens by recalling the field that carried you over the gap, then states the departure outright: "There is no stored velocity here." The reader knows what has changed and why.
reading.handover_out: Clean on the receiving side. Forge ends "The next sequence begins with oscillation. A form can persist through returning motion as well as through rest", and WaveFunctions_Intro opens on a bob that keeps leaving its ring and recalls "position, velocity and force in earlier rooms". The weakness is on Forge's side: at 543 words it hands over before gathering the sequence's six operations or restating its truth.
reading_errors: stumbles: "the tremble inset can be read as a running solver" — the inset says otherwise in the hall: settling_tremble.gd:42 tags it "analytic catenary / fixed offsets" and :46 prints "seeded offsets within +/- epsilon, not solver output / fixed points / magnified differences / no motion". The chapter is silent about it; the object is not.

holds[3]: "no compatible live measurement" is presented as the shared science_screen coda in four halls, but that phrase is Catenary's only (final.md:48). Equilibrium :44 says "no live load measurement", Relaxation :44 and Annealing :47 say different things. Four halls carry a screen coda; they do not share the sentence. (Descent's map also places a science_screen at (10,23) with no coda in the chapter.)

hall_notes FormFinding_Relaxation: the wind-off figures are described as numbers "the live readout will not show". The readout shows them: WIND toggles and restarts the run (verlet_workbench.gd:414-421), the step counter starts at 60 (:241), and MEAN/WORST print at :332-334 — they are simply not the default view. The stumbles entry states it correctly ("on the driven live readout").

hall_notes word counts (1015 / 976 / 911 / 965 / 1051 / 543) do not match wc -w on the six files (1039 / 1036 / 966 / 1031 / 1104 / 552). The ordering and the "half the length" claim about Forge hold; the figures are a different counting method and should not be quoted as measured word counts without saying which.

arc: "Forge closes on a detector" — the detector (balance_puzzle) is the hall's first anchor and opens the chapter (final.md:5-13); the chapter closes on an instruction about the puzzle (:25) and then the oscillation handover (:27). Defensible as a reading, inexact as a description of order.

tasks.title: The vessel now has a collider; the chapter invites you to walk through it
tasks.spec:
[code-claim] FormFinding_Relaxation
Quote: “The glass does not contain you: it has no collider, so your body can walk through its wall.”
Why: In the working tree the vessel builds a StaticBody3D trimesh skin with backface collision, its label says "closed skin", and the registry says it carries two-sided surface collision; a headset visitor who takes the sentence literally walks into a wall. Both the collider and this sentence are uncommitted: HEAD's chapter (:36) made the same no-collider claim in other words and it was true of HEAD's body-less vessel; the current wave rewrote the sentence and added the skin without reconciling them.
Do: Decide which vessel ships. If the closed skin stays (registry and label already say so), rewrite: "It has a collider and no mouth: your hand and body stop at its wall, and the inside you can see through the glass is not a place you can enter." If the walkable vessel is the intent, revert the FrozenSkin block and the registry line instead. Commit whichever wins so chapter, code and registry agree.

tasks.title: Four retained comparison works stand behind the lab with no words
tasks.spec:
[encounter] FormFinding_Descent
Quote: “Behind this experiment, the retained marble toy carries velocity and receives periodic programmed kicks.”
Why: Five works stand between the spawn and the exit and the chapter names one in half a sentence: a Perlin-terrain descent station, a glowing "How I learned" well that the book calls the hall's hero, a science screen, and a static inset of a sampled catenary with seeded offsets. The inset's own plaque already says "not solver output / no motion", so the visitor is told by the object but not by the book; the other three get nothing at all, and Descent is the only hall with a screen on the floor and no screen coda in the chapter.
Do: A short anchored "Comparisons" passage after "The surface we agreed to search", one sentence each: the marble (velocity, damping, a kick every five seconds, a swaying bowl); the terrain station (the same finite-difference descent on seeded Perlin ground with its own threshold and a 160-step budget); the well (marbles that fall, settle, pulse and begin again — a portrait, not an instrument); the tremble inset (a sampled curve with fixed seeded offsets magnified eight times, and its plaque says so). Close with the one-line science_screen coda the other four halls use.
Evidence: commons/maps/FormFinding_Descent/map_data.json interactables (10,17) settling_tremble, (5,19) descent_marble_toy, (9,21) gradient_descent, (4,23) gradient_descent_well, (10,23) science_screen; utilities spawn (2,18), t (11,25); commons/artifacts/descent_marble_toy/descent_marble_toy.gd:136-137 (accel, 0.985 damping), :143-145 (kick every 5 s), :149-150 (sway); algorithms/formfinding/settling_tremble/settling_tremble.gd:42, :46 (in-world labels), :67 (mag 8.0); algorithms/machinelearning/gradientdescent/GradientDescentDemo.gd:32 (noise_seed), :43 (max_steps 160), :76 (TYPE_PERLIN); commons/artifacts/registry/formfinding.json:9, machinelearning.json:3637, self_portrait.json:56; commons/data/book/formfinding.json pearls[0].hero = "gradient_descent_well"; tools/artifact_roles.py --brief --seq formfinding.

tasks.title: Make the MEAN/WORST figures reproducible from the bench, not from a desktop run
tasks.spec:
[vr] FormFinding_Relaxation
Quote: “In a matched desktop calculation after 420 total undriven steps—sixty preliminary steps and 360 more—one pass leaves a mean absolute error of about 1.409% and a worst spring error of 34.276%.”
Why: Besides the desktop aside, the live MEAN and WORST the visitor was just told to read will not show these numbers by default: WIND is on, so the readout is driven, and only the step counter tells you when 420 has passed. Told how to reproduce it, the visitor can check the claim in the headset; the step counter starts at 60, so 420 is what it will read.
Do: "Switch WIND off; the cloth restarts from its sixty preliminary steps (RESET does the same without changing a setting). When the step count reads 420, about six seconds later, one pass leaves a mean error of about 1.4% and a worst spring error of about 34%; four passes bring those to about 0.36% and 8.9%." (Keep the three-decimal figures if you prefer; the readout shows two.)
